title: Take payment
$idempotencyComment: Square's window is 24 hours, and the key is a REQUIRED body field rather than a header. `required` makes the generated executor derive it from the RUN and the NODE -- never fresh -- so a resumed durable run returns the original payment instead of taking a second one.

config.label: Payment source
config.description: A payment token from the Web Payments SDK, a saved card id, or CASH / EXTERNAL. Square calls it source_id.

config.label: Amount
config.description: In the currency's smallest unit — 1000 is $10.00. Square has no decimal amounts, exactly like Stripe.

send.error: "amount" must be a positive whole number in the currency's smallest unit (1000 = $10.00)

config.label: Currency
config.description: Three-letter ISO code. Square wants it UPPERCASE, where Stripe wants it lowercase — the same field, opposite conventions.

config.label: Location
config.description: Which of the seller's locations the payment belongs to. Square scopes almost everything by location.

config.label: Reference
config.description: Your own id for this payment. The usual way to find it again later.

outputShape.description: Which estate this ran against: fake, sandbox or live.
The connection id that was used.
Square's payment id. NESTED under `payment` — Square wraps its responses where Stripe returns the object at the top level.
Amount in the currency's smallest unit.
A hosted receipt Square generates for the buyer.
Present when Square accepted the request and refused the payment. Check it before treating a 200 as money taken.
